title: Deeper/broader source-distinct C++ DWG parser and 2D projection candidate review
mode: primary-source web research and read-only local plan review
scope: Search for a newly surfaced source-distinct DWG/DXF implementation in C++, the language used by libdxfrw
Check its license, format/version claims, parser-to-consumer boundary, test evidence, and upstream knowledge lineage
Update optional peer admission without changing implementation order, fast validation, or support claims

method.kind: Read the project repository, current V1 plan, architecture, type reference, and superseded historical status
method.limitations: Reviewed GitHub main/docs are mutable and no exact commit, release artifact, compiler profile, executable, or public DWG corpus was acquired. PROJECT_STATUS.md states it is superseded. The reviewed sources do not establish a full source-lineage audit, current parity, or per-file results.

sources.revision: Mutable main/repository page reviewed 2026-10-18; no release listed in the reviewed repository page
sources.observed: The project identifies an MIT license and a C++20 core, advertises a self-developed DWG/DXF parser, lists R2000/R2004/R2007/R2010/R2013/R2018 DWG families, and routes results to a SceneGraph and JSON/2D rendering pipeline. No writer capability was established by the reviewed page.

The V1 plan names LibreDWG as source-only/read-only material for format understanding, not a linked product dependency. Architecture documents byte-to-SceneGraph parsing and a normalized render projection. The reviewed object-type list names generic SOLID but does not establish DWG 3DSOLID/ACIS payload decoding, AcDs association, a B-rep kernel, raw-object retention, or writer paths.

sources.project: ft_model superseded historical status and public test-reference tree
sources.revision: Mutable main documentation/tree reviewed 2026-10-18; status document says it is historical and superseded
sources.observed: The old status report records R2004 object-map loss, missing version-family fixtures, partial layout/reference behavior, and parser corrections involving object-map reset, CMC, string streams, EED alignment, and LWPOLYLINE extrusion. It also references a historical LibreDWG algorithm path. These are dated maintainer disclosures, not current-main failures or libdxfrw defects. The reviewed test_reference directory listed only .gitignore; named real DWG sentinels were not available for reproduction from the reviewed public tree.

sources.project: Existing libdxfrw peer matrix and evidence rules
sources.revision: Working tree over baseline de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9 reviewed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: Existing plan gates require exact artifact/profile and independent expected values; local per-slice validation is already focused. The candidate is therefore recorded only as an optional source-distinct, reference-correlated common-2D projection route.

assessment.planImpact: Adds ft_model to the peer matrix as an optional, source-distinct but LibreDWG-reference-correlated common-2D DWG projection candidate only. It is not a writer, raw record/graph preservation, ACIS/AcDs, B-rep, native acceptance, or support oracle. No required gate or implementation action was added.

implementationReadyChecks: Do not add ft_model as a CMake/CI dependency or execute it during ordinary implementation slices.
For a future named common-2D question only, pin source commit/tree digest, build/toolchain, platform, options, input hash/provenance, and diagnostics.
Use a locally authored expected manifest and generated controls or already-authorized local fixtures; do not copy peer/customer DWG/DXF files or self-reported expected outputs.
Compare only fields and identities the candidate actually exposes; report unobservable fields as unavailable, not as matched or zero.
Keep normalized geometry projection separate from raw records, graph/owner closure, writer output, ACIS/AcDs association, B-rep semantics, and native CAD acceptance.
Keep findings/subplans at 130/73 and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 DEFERRED_EXTERNAL.
